bull_bear.body:
- Well-recognised, long-established brand (since 1986) with strong customer acceptance and distinctive designs, ranking among the top kitchen appliances manufacturers in India
- Diversified product portfolio spanning core cooking appliances and alternate/auxiliary categories (chimneys, flasks, kettles, sandwich makers)
- Multi-channel distribution reach - offline including large-format retail, online (including new entry into q-commerce), and alternate channels - supporting market-share gains across core categories
- Majority ownership by and association with Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals Limited (75% holding company), bringing engineering expertise, scale and pan-India distribution reach
- Strong credit profile - CRISIL AA/Stable (long-term) and CRISIL A1+ (short-term) bank facility ratings reaffirmed unchanged during the year, reflecting financial resilience
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material and input cost volatility — Rising costs of metals, plastics and electronic components pressure margins; elevated global commodity prices and a weakening rupee increased input costs during FY26 and led to gradual price increases in Q4.
- Intensifying competition — Influx of new domestic and international brands across price points is intensifying competition in the kitchen appliances category, increasing both price and innovation pressure.
- Channel fragmentation and online promotional intensity — Growing promotional intensity on online marketplaces and channel fragmentation are compressing margins and increasing revenue volatility as distribution shifts toward online/e-commerce.
- Regulatory compliance and supply-chain volatility — Regulatory requirements such as energy labelling, safety and environmental norms, combined with supply-chain volatility, are increasing compliance costs and lead times.
- Macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty — A weakening rupee, geopolitical tensions and global trade uncertainty affect input costs and demand momentum; management flagged sustaining growth amid these dynamics as a key consideration, with Q4 FY26 demand notably volatile.
- Litigation, claims and uncertain tax positions — The Company discloses exposure to a variety of laws, regulations, positions and interpretations - including direct taxation matters - creating contingent legal and tax risk (Board's Report, 'Risk arising out of litigation, claims and uncertain tax positions').
- Broad multi-category enterprise risk exposure — The Board-approved Risk Management Policy itself identifies strategic, financial, credit, market, liquidity, security, property, legal and regulatory risk as elements the Company may face, indicating a wide risk surface actively overseen by the Risk Management Committee.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Established in 1986, Butterfly is a leading player in the Indian appliances industry and a well-recognised brand in South India, ranking among the top kitchen appliances manufacturers in the country. It manufactures and sells a diverse portfolio of kitchen and domestic electrical appliances - LPG stoves, mixer grinders, pressure cookers, tabletop wet grinders, chimneys, air fryers, kettles, sandwich makers, inductions and flasks - through a distribution mix of distributors, retailers, institutional buyers and large-format stores, supported by a growing online/q-commerce presence, largely within India with a small export footprint.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Build future growth platforms under 'lifestyle-tech' and wellness themes to address emerging premium consumer needs, governed through a structured innovation pipeline with KPIs for new-product contribution, premium mix and technology adoption
- Maintain a disciplined portfolio and price-value architecture across entry, mid and premium segments to avoid price-led competition and protect margins amid intensifying domestic and international competition
- Institute a quarterly pricing strategy with key raw-material suppliers - starting with the top 3 contributors before extending to the next level of suppliers - to gain visibility and mitigate raw-material price volatility
- Strengthen a resilient, value-led and diversified portfolio focused on essential-use and replacement-driven categories to stay relevant during periods of constrained consumer spending
- Reduce demand risk through portfolio, channel and market diversification, including expansion to the rest of India and the D2C segment
- Reinforce brand trust and reliability through post-purchase support (Butterfly Assist+) and sustained marketing investment behind the 'Celebrating Change' brand transformation
- Continue fortifying the digital backbone - SD-WAN network architecture, deeper integration with Crompton's enterprise technology ecosystem, and strengthened cybersecurity (DLP, MDM, XDR, SIEM/SOC, Zero Trust) - to support future expansion
- Pursue a structured, continuous data-privacy readiness journey (DPIAs, governance strengthening) aligned with India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) framework rather than one-time compliance
- Re-engineer manufacturing planning through an M+1 framework and advance multi-sourcing/localisation across the supply chain to reduce dependency risk and improve visibility for long-lead components
- The Company's Dividend Distribution Policy (formulated under SEBI LODR Regulation 43A, effective from April 2, 2020) determines pay-out based on standalone/net operating profit after tax, operating cash flow, liquidity position and aggregate debt/debt-service coverage, loan repayment and working-capital requirements, capital expenditure requirements, and resources needed for funding acquisitions or mergers, rather than a fixed payout ratio. In line with this philosophy, the Board decided not to recommend any dividend for FY2025-26, with a stated view of conserving resources to support future growth and expansion.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY26, the Company completed consolidation of one manufacturing facility into its main plant, deployed automation lines, strengthened shop-floor quality systems and enhanced vendor/supplier collaboration. With plant consolidation completed, the next phase focuses on automation and capacity readiness, with production planning being aligned to support anticipated growth, including a planned expansion of pressure cooker capacity from around 12 Lakh units towards 18 Lakh units. The Company operates a 25+ acre campus with an integrated manufacturing facility housing its dedicated in-house R&D team for product design and development. During the year it introduced an M+1 manufacturing planning framework for earlier finalisation of confirmed/tentative production plans and advanced multi-sourcing and localisation across the supply chain to reduce dependency risk on key inputs. Manufacturing teams adopted multi-operation tooling (in collaboration with R&D and tooling partners) to handle the greater tooling and process complexity of the Idea First Series, improving productivity and throughput. The Company also achieved India's first five-star energy-efficiency certification for cooktops during the year, and reported quality improvements including a reduction in Parts Per Rejection (PPR) from 9.24 to 8.39 and Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) from 1.93 to 1.80. On the BRSR environmental/social capex-allocation disclosure, the Company reported that 30.31% of its capex (down from 41.36% in FY25) and 69.69% of its R&D spend (up from 58.64% in FY25) went toward technologies improving environmental and social impact of products/processes. Supporting sustainability initiatives, the Company also shifted to group captive solar power, generating measurable energy-cost savings.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Growing demand for smart and connected appliances - app-enabled control, voice-assisted operation and energy-monitoring features - reshaping traditional product categories
- Rising disposable incomes and expanding consumer base: India's PFCE grew 7.5% in FY26 (up from 7.2%); GST rationalisation and tax relief on select consumer durables expected to support affordability and discretionary consumption; small domestic appliances market projected to grow at a 7.42% CAGR between 2026 and 2031
- Higher consumption in Tier II/III cities driving distribution-led category expansion; online retail projected to grow at an 8.45% CAGR aided by deeper Tier II/III penetration and fintech-enabled affordability
- Shift towards convenience-driven consumption benefiting mixers, blenders, kettles, air fryers and food processors, with juicers and blenders accounting for 21.86% of the market in 2025
- Preference for energy-efficient products reinforced by BEE-linked efficiency norms and localisation incentives
- Expanding e-commerce and omnichannel retail - multi-brand outlets held the largest share (46.62%) in 2025, but online retail expected to grow faster at an 8.45% CAGR
- Government electrification and housing initiatives (PMAY, rural electrification) expanding the addressable consumer base for kitchen appliances
- Rapid growth expected in small/compact appliances such as air fryers, projected at a 7.88% CAGR through 2031
- India's consumer durables market projected to become the fourth largest globally by FY2026-27
- Company-level outlook: innovation-driven product launches, emphasis on alternate appliances, targeted consumer outreach and continuous spend optimisation are stated to position the Company to sustain growth in both revenue and profitability going forward
- FY26 growth was driven across all quarters by the brand refresh and Idea First Series launch, supported by ATL/digital campaigns and retail visibility drives; EBITDA improvement attributed to spend optimisation, distributor-margin restructuring and improved product mix despite higher ad spend
